A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RDIRL work. All 17 pages of v5 and 21 pages of v6, including the appendices, support matching the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 and Appendix B.5.1 report original continuous-control, cognitive-radar and online-baseline experiments, with numerical results and learning curves.

after.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 and Appendix B.3 retain those original experiments and their numerical results and learning curves.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 now computes the current inverse-Hessian matrix before using it in the parameter update, correcting v5's reversed pseudocode order. The underlying moment-matching objective, recursive update equations and inner-policy optimization remain the same.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CartPole, MountainCar, HalfCheetah-v4, Hopper, Walker2d and cognitive radar, including the same streaming comparisons. Expanded radar descriptions do not establish a new task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained: SQIL, GAIL, GCL, AIRL and ML-IRL in Table 1; GAIL, GCL and AIRL for radar and Walker2d; and the same four online-adapted baselines in the appendix.

E3.justification: Expert generation, state-only demonstrations, MPPI-based comparisons, episode budgets and Table 3 hyperparameters are retained. The expanded radar setup supplies previously unstated details without establishing a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The online-adaptation analysis in v5 Appendix B.5.1 is retained as v6 Appendix B.3, including Figure 4 and Table 4. No new ablations, robustness tests or empirical supplementary analyses appear.

E5.justification: Both report 12 Monte Carlo runs with different seeds for continuous control and five for radar, retaining the same uncertainty-reporting practice. The changed Table 1 uncertainty value does not introduce a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SQIL's MountainCar entry from -0.001 ± 4.79 to -0.001 ± 4.79 × 10^-5. Other benchmark and online-adaptation table results and all four learning-curve figures are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds explicit bounded-cost and bounded-density conditions, Lemma 4.1 establishing parameter-independent bounds, and a derivation allowing unequal expert/background sample counts. The recursive proof is expanded in Section 5; its underlying derivation already appeared in v5 Appendix B.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and principal conclusion retain the claims of online neural cost learning through a moment-matching upper bound, recursive second-order updates and faster benchmark convergence. No new primary contribution is claimed.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 5 reinterpret RDIRL as approximate Newton optimization, distinguishing inverse-Hessian step scaling and regularization from Kalman covariance and process noise. New discussion addresses bound tightness and full-Hessian scaling, with larger-network approximations left to future work.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 substantially expands radar implementation details with dynamics, timestep, signal and noise parameters, relative-displacement network inputs and output ReLU. Existing architecture, hardware, training-time, hyperparameter and code-availability disclosures remain; these additions do not establish rerun experiments.

R1.justification: V6 adds Zhang et al. (2018), Gupta et al. (2018) and Anil et al. (2020) to support proposed scalable Hessian approximations. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Background and bound explanations are extensively expanded. Appendix B.3–B.4 material is reorganized into main-text Sections 5.1–5.3, and the radar section gains separate expert and target descriptions. Publication headers and acknowledgments are also updated.

P2.justification: The journal format changes typography and text width, separates the title page from the abstract, reformats Algorithm 1 and all tables, and replaces crowded wrapped displays with centered figures. Figure 4 and Table 4 are colocated; plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: V6 improves v5's underspecified bound conditions, optimizer explanation and radar documentation. However, new Equations 43–44 define a log-determinant reward using a rank-one 3D FIM, without stated regularization or accumulation to explain the finite rewards in Table 2. These documentation gains coexist with an unresolved mathematical inconsistency in an important evaluation, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
